home-remodeling.local_heading: Where the pavement stops, the acreage starts
intro_paragraphs: Southwest Ranches is thirteen square miles of one-acre-and-up parcels that voted itself into existence in 2000 rather than get absorbed by a neighbor. The housing follows: long low ranch houses from the 1970s and 80s in Sunshine Ranches and Green Meadows, and custom estates built since the 1990s along Holatee Trail, Appaloosa Trail and inside Landmark Ranch Estates. What owners here ask for is not a smaller footprint. It is a whole-home remodel that opens the plan, replaces forty-year-old mechanicals, and finally makes the house match the land around it.

Everything gets permitted through the Town of Southwest Ranches, whose building division sits at Town Hall on Griffin Road, runs plan review and inspections under contract, and takes every submittal electronically. Two things surprise owners arriving from Miami-Dade. The Broward County Board of Rules and Appeals adopts the county amendments to the Florida Building Code and certifies the officials who will review and inspect your job. And Broward sits inside the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone as well, so every window, door and roof assembly needs an HVHZ product approval. Well and septic parcels bring the Florida Department of Health in Broward County into it too.

A remodel on an acre is a logistics problem as much as a construction one. Crews come down a long private drive, material stages where it will not crush a swale or block the right-of-way trail, and the site stays orderly because every neighbor can see all of it. The scope is agreed in writing and priced before anything is demolished, one supervisor runs the job every day it is open, and the same team answers for it from estimate through warranty. Twenty-plus years in South Florida, 150-plus remodels and additions delivered, all permitted and inspected.
home-remodeling.scope_intro: The scope is settled on paper before a crew ever reaches the driveway. Below is the work a whole-home remodel on Ranches acreage normally carries.

scope_items.name: Opening the ranch plan
scope_items.desc: Dropping walls between the kitchen, family room and Florida room, with engineered beams and sealed calculations so a 1970s bearing wall can leave quietly.

scope_items.name: Well water, treated properly
scope_items.desc: Whole-house filtration, softening and iron treatment sized to your well, because hard water quietly ruins new fixtures, glass and stone faster than anything else.

scope_items.name: HVHZ windows and doors
scope_items.desc: Impact glass and exterior doors carrying High-Velocity Hurricane Zone approvals, installed with the anchoring detail the Broward inspector will actually check.

scope_items.name: Plumbing, drains and septic load
scope_items.desc: New supply and drain lines throughout, plus an honest look at whether the added fixtures push your septic system past what it was permitted to carry.

faqs.q: Who issues the building permit for a remodel in Southwest Ranches?
faqs.a: The Town of Southwest Ranches does, through its building permitting and inspections division at Town Hall on Griffin Road, with plan review and inspection services provided under contract by CAP Government. Applications and drawings are submitted electronically, and the Town also uses Broward County's E-Permits arrangement, so associated county approvals can move alongside the town permit instead of behind it. We prepare and file the whole package, then chase the corrections.

faqs.q: How does the county Board of Rules and Appeals review my plans?
faqs.a: It does not review your plans, and that confusion is common. BORA is Broward's countywide code-administration body: it adopts the Broward amendments to the Florida Building Code, certifies the building officials, plans examiners and inspectors working in the county, issues formal code interpretations, and hears appeals of a code official's decision. Practically, it shapes what your reviewer expects to see, and it is one of the genuine differences between building in Broward and building in Miami-Dade.

faqs.q: My house is on a well and septic. Does that change a whole-home remodel?
faqs.a: It changes the sequence and the questions. Most of Southwest Ranches is served by private wells and onsite septic rather than city water and sewer, so before we design new baths or a bigger kitchen we look at the existing septic permit, the drainfield and reserve area, and the well location. Adding fixtures can require a modification permit from the Florida Department of Health in Broward County. Water treatment then gets specified around what your well actually produces.

faqs.q: How long does a whole-home remodel take out here?
faqs.a: Plan in quarters, not weeks. Design and engineering come first, then town review; the Town's own guidance puts residential construction permits in a fifteen-to-thirty working day window for a response, and revisions add cycles. Construction on a large single-story estate commonly runs six months to a year, longer if you are also re-roofing or moving the septic. A written schedule comes with the estimate, and somebody on site owns it.

faqs.q: How much should we set aside for a full remodel?
faqs.a: Square footage out here is the first shock: a 6,000-square-foot ranch costs more to gut than a small bungalow, and the mechanical runs are longer. Beyond that, the number depends on selections and on what the house is hiding. We scope it in writing with real allowances rather than a hopeful headline figure. PGX competes on certainty and finish, not on being the low bid, and we say so before you spend money on drawings.

home-remodeling.cta_sub: Bring the survey, the septic permit if you have it, and the wish list. You will leave with a real scope and a real number, in English o en español.

kitchen-remodeling.hero_sub: Custom cabinetry, stone counters and real layout changes for Southwest Ranches kitchens, including the well-water treatment and propane work nobody mentions. Permitted through the Town and supervised daily by a licensed general contractor.
kitchen-remodeling.local_heading: The kitchen at the end of the driveway
intro_paragraphs: Estate kitchens in Southwest Ranches were mostly drawn for a different life. The 1970s and 80s ranch houses across Green Meadows, Country Estates and Rolling Oaks came with a galley tucked behind a wall, one wall oven, and a pantry the size of a coat closet, inside a house clearly built to host. So the projects here run large: absorb the adjoining den, set a long island, add a scullery and a second dishwasher, and build the cold storage a family who shops once a week actually needs.

Nothing here is exempt: plumbing, gas, electrical and usually structure mean a permit from the Town of Southwest Ranches and inspections along the way, submitted electronically like everything else here. Interior-only work skips site-plan review; move an exterior wall or add a window and zoning looks first. Two local wrinkles: any new opening needs a High-Velocity Hurricane Zone product approval, since Broward is in the HVHZ alongside Miami-Dade, and adding a second dishwasher or a disposal on a septic property deserves a look at the system's permitted capacity.

Cabinet packages and stone slabs do not enjoy a mile of two-lane road and a gravel drive, so delivery and staging get planned like part of the build. We template stone after cabinets are set, never before. Selections are locked into a fixed written scope, a supervisor is on site every day, and the rest of the house stays sealed off and clean while the kitchen is open. Licensed and insured under Lic. CGC1539072, with 150-plus remodels and additions delivered across South Florida, all of them permitted.
kitchen-remodeling.scope_intro: Every line is drawn and priced before a cabinet leaves the wall. These are the items that show up most in acreage kitchens west of Flamingo Road.

scope_items.name: Cabinet runs made to fit
scope_items.desc: Built-to-order cabinet runs finished for Florida humidity, scaled to the walls and ceiling heights you actually have instead of chopped into stock boxes.

scope_items.name: Islands built for slab weight
scope_items.desc: Quartzite, marble or granite templated in place, over framing built for the slab weight and for overhangs people will genuinely sit on.

scope_items.name: Walls out, beams in
scope_items.desc: Removing the wall between kitchen and living space, with the beam, columns and sealed engineering the Town will want to see before demolition.

scope_items.name: Propane, hoods and venting
scope_items.desc: Ranges fed from a buried propane tank where there is no gas main, with makeup air and hood runs sized properly rather than symbolically.

scope_items.name: Water worth drinking
scope_items.desc: Filtration, softening and reverse osmosis at the sink and the ice maker, because well water and a new stone counter are not natural allies.

faqs.q: Is a permit required for a kitchen out here?
faqs.a: For anything past paint and appliance swaps, yes. Moving plumbing, adding circuits, running a gas or propane line, or taking out a wall all require a permit from the Town and inspections before things get closed up. Applications go in electronically. Unpermitted kitchen work tends to surface during a sale or an insurance inspection, and permitting it after the fact costs more than doing it once.

faqs.q: We are on a well. Will the water damage a new kitchen?
faqs.a: Untreated well water will absolutely leave its mark: iron staining on a farmhouse sink, scale on the faucet and the ice maker, cloudy film on marble and glass. It is fixable and worth fixing before the finishes go in. We specify whole-house filtration and softening sized to your well, plus point-of-use reverse osmosis for drinking and ice. Good water is the cheapest way to protect an expensive kitchen.

faqs.q: Can I have a gas range if there is no gas line to my house?
faqs.a: Usually yes, with propane. Plenty of Southwest Ranches properties sit beyond a natural gas main, so the answer is a buried or screened tank feeding the range, the cooktop and sometimes the pool heater and generator. Tank placement has setback rules, the line gets permitted and pressure tested, and the hood and makeup air get sized for the burner output rather than for the photograph.

faqs.q: How long will a custom kitchen take?
faqs.a: Cabinetry sets the clock. A made-to-order package runs months in fabrication, which is why we order early and time demolition to the delivery date instead of leaving you without a kitchen while a factory catches up. On-site work is usually a couple of months, longer when a bearing wall or a new propane run is involved. Permitting adds weeks on the front end, and we build that into the written schedule.

faqs.q: Where does a Ranches kitchen budget actually go?
faqs.a: Cabinetry, stone and appliances drive the number, and Ranches kitchens tend to be large, which multiplies all three. Add the unglamorous items an acreage property brings: water treatment, a propane run, sometimes a panel upgrade. Rather than float a range that means nothing, we walk the space, write a specification, and price it. We are not the cheapest bid in the driveway, and we will tell you that early.

kitchen-remodeling.cta_sub: Show us the room, the appliance list and the way you actually cook. You get a written specification and a price that holds, in English o en español.

bathroom-remodeling.local_heading: Two baths for a five-bedroom ranch
intro_paragraphs: The math never worked. A 1980s ranch on two acres in Sunshine Ranches or Santa Fe Estates typically came with a compartmentalized primary bath, a tub nobody has filled in twenty years, and a hall bath doing far too much work. Owners here fix it by taking territory: annexing a bedroom or the outsized closet, building a wet room with a freestanding tub and a walk-in shower, then adding a proper pool bath so wet feet stop crossing the marble. On acreage, there is usually room to do it right.

Bath permits come from the Town of Southwest Ranches, with plumbing, electrical and mechanical inspections before tile hides anything. The part that catches people is downstream: most of the town runs on onsite septic rather than sewer, so adding fixtures can push a system past its permitted load and require review by the Florida Department of Health in Broward County, which also handles the well. If the scope touches an exterior wall or a new window, HVHZ product approvals apply, because Broward sits inside the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone.

Everything expensive in a bathroom sits on top of something invisible. Membranes get flood-tested before tile, slopes get verified with a level, blocking goes in behind every grab bar and glass panel, and exhaust gets ducted outside rather than into the attic. Slab work goes to fabricators who have been cutting book-matched stone for decades. You get the scope in writing, daily supervision, and protected pathways from the front door to the work zone, because a bathroom project should not redecorate the rest of the house.
bathroom-remodeling.scope_heading: What a Ranches bath remodel includes
bathroom-remodeling.scope_intro: Nothing gets ordered until the drawing and the specification agree. Below are the elements that repeat across acreage bathrooms in this town.

scope_items.name: Taking the adjacent bedroom
scope_items.desc: Turning a spare bedroom or an oversized closet into the suite the original plan never allowed, with framing, rough-in and drawings resolved before demolition.

scope_items.name: Wet rooms and curbless entries
scope_items.desc: Recessed pans cut into slab where the structure allows, linear drains, and heavy glass anchored to real blocking so nothing shifts in year three.

scope_items.name: Waterproofing you never see
scope_items.desc: Bonded membranes, sealed corners and a flood test held overnight before tile, since the only cheap time to catch a leak is now.

scope_items.name: Fixture count and septic
scope_items.desc: A straight answer on whether new fixtures exceed what your onsite system was permitted for, and coordination of any Health Department review that follows.

scope_items.name: Stone that survives the water
scope_items.desc: Marble and quartzite sealed for a hard-water house, with fixtures and finishes chosen so mineral staining does not become the room's main feature.

faqs.q: Can our septic handle another bathroom?
faqs.a: It might, and that is worth knowing before design rather than after. Onsite systems are permitted for a certain load, based on bedrooms and fixtures, and a new full bath or a converted bonus room can exceed it. We pull the existing septic permit, locate the tank, drainfield and reserve area, and if the system needs modification we coordinate the application with the Florida Department of Health in Broward County. Sometimes the answer is simply yes, no changes needed.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for a bathroom remodel here?
faqs.a: Yes for anything structural, plumbing, electrical or ventilation related, which is essentially any real remodel. The Town issues the permit and inspects the rough work before it disappears behind tile, and that sequence protects you: someone besides your contractor confirmed the waterproofing and the rough plumbing. Cosmetic swaps like paint, a mirror or a like-for-like vanity change generally do not. We pull permits, book inspections and hand you the closed-out paperwork.

faqs.q: Our well water leaves orange stains. Can that be solved before we tile?
faqs.a: Yes, and it should be. Iron, hardness and sulfur are common in private wells across western Broward, and they will find your new fixtures, glass and stone within months. The fix is a properly sized treatment train at the house, not a filter under the sink, plus finishes and hardware selected knowing what the water is. We would rather solve it during the remodel than watch a beautiful bathroom stain on schedule.

faqs.q: Can we live in the house while the primary bath is rebuilt?
faqs.a: Usually, and Ranches houses make it easier than most because there is normally another bathroom far enough away to be usable. We seal the work zone, run negative air where dust is a concern, protect the route from the driveway, and keep at least one bathroom online throughout. The stretch you will feel is the plumbing shutdown, which we schedule and keep short. If it ever makes sense to leave, we say so.

faqs.q: What does a primary suite bath cost at this level?
faqs.a: Stone, glass, fixtures and the labor to install them carefully carry most of it, and the invisible half, meaning waterproofing, new drains, venting and any septic coordination, is the part people forget to budget. We will not throw out a number before seeing the space. After a walk-through you get a written scope and a fixed price. We build at a high-end standard and price accordingly, which we say up front.

home-additions.hero_sub: Rear extensions, guest houses, in-law suites and second stories on Southwest Ranches acreage, engineered around your drainfield and setbacks, permitted through the Town, and built under daily supervision by a licensed general contractor.
home-additions.local_heading: Room to build, rules to respect
intro_paragraphs: Nobody buys in Southwest Ranches to feel cramped, and yet the houses are often the small thing on a big parcel. Adding on is the obvious move: a rear wing with a primary suite behind a ranch in Rolling Oaks, a guest house for parents or a trainer near the barn, a second story on a house in Ivanhoe Estates where the owners want a view of their own pasture. Because lots here start at an acre and run to five, the constraint is rarely land. It is septic, setbacks and drainage.

An addition clears zoning and site-plan review at the Town of Southwest Ranches before the building application moves, and the Town's engineering side issues fill, excavation and grading permits where work could affect floodplain storage, a real concern on the eastern edge of the Everglades. You cannot build over a drainfield or its reserve area, so the septic layout often decides the footprint. Guest houses are allowed but regulated: one per parcel, no full kitchen, no separate meter or mailing address, and buildings housing animals carry their own yard requirement.

Out here the hard part is not land, it is the seam between old structure and new. Tying a new foundation to a forty-year-old one, matching stucco texture and roof tile so the seam disappears, upgrading tie-beams, keeping the occupied half of the house sealed, warm and quiet while the other half is open sky. PGX runs it as one contract with one supervisor, a fixed written scope, and a schedule you can hold us to. Twenty-plus years in South Florida, licensed and insured, and every project permitted and inspected from footing to final.
home-additions.scope_intro: Every one starts with a survey, the septic layout and a structural engineer. Five shapes cover most of what gets built out here.

scope_items.name: New wings on acreage
scope_items.desc: Extending into the yard for a primary suite, great room or home office, with new footings, tie-beam work and roof tie-ins engineered before pricing.

scope_items.name: Guest houses and in-law suites
scope_items.desc: Detached or attached quarters built to the Town's guesthouse rules, which cap one per parcel, forbid a full kitchen and set a floor-area limit by lot size.

scope_items.name: Going up over the estate
scope_items.desc: A structural evaluation of the existing walls and footings first, then a real upper floor with stair placement that does not wreck the plan below.

scope_items.name: Garage and barn conversions
scope_items.desc: Turning an oversized garage or an unused accessory building into conditioned space, done legally so the square footage counts when the property changes hands.

scope_items.name: Septic, well and drainage work
scope_items.desc: Relocating or upgrading the onsite system where the addition demands it, plus the grading and fill permits the Town requires when floodplain storage is touched.

faqs.q: Can I build a guest house on my Southwest Ranches property?
faqs.a: Often, within limits, and the limits are specific. The town's code allows one guesthouse per parcel, and it cannot be sold or leased separately, cannot have a full kitchen, and cannot carry its own mailing address or electric meter. It is not permitted on parcels under 35,000 square feet, and floor area is capped, more tightly on a one-acre parcel than on a larger one. Placement still has to respect setbacks, the drainfield and reserve area, and the well. We check the parcel against the survey before anyone draws.

faqs.q: How does septic limit where I can put an addition?
faqs.a: More than most owners expect. The tank, the drainfield and the unobstructed reserve area all need to stay clear, so a slab cannot go over them and heavy equipment should not roll across them either. Setback distances to the well matter too. Sometimes the addition simply shifts twenty feet; sometimes the system gets relocated or upgraded, which is its own permit through the Florida Department of Health in Broward County. We resolve this at survey stage, not at foundation stage.

faqs.q: Is there a design review board I have to satisfy?
faqs.a: Southwest Ranches does not run an architectural board the way some coastal cities do. What it does enforce is zoning: lot coverage, setbacks, height, accessory structure rules, and the rural character the town incorporated in 2000 to protect. Site plan and land use items go before the Town's planning process, engineering reviews grading and right-of-way work, and the building permit follows. If your parcel sits in a platted community with its own covenants, those apply on top.

faqs.q: How long from first sketch to finished addition?
faqs.a: Front-load the calendar. Survey, design, structural engineering, septic verification and town review commonly take several months before a shovel moves, and revisions add cycles. Construction on a substantial rear wing or a second story typically runs six months or more once permitted. A year from first conversation to move-in is a fair expectation for a real addition. You get the whole sequence in writing, with the slow parts labeled honestly.

faqs.q: Does adding on beat buying a bigger house out here?
faqs.a: Frequently, because the land is the expensive part and you already own it. Acreage in this town is finite and the trails, the zoning and the quiet are exactly what people pay for. Building the wing you are missing usually costs less than trading up and moving, and it keeps the parcel you chose. It is still real construction with real disruption, so it suits owners planning to stay. Come to us with the idea and we will tell you honestly whether the parcel supports it.

home-additions.cta_sub: Send the survey and the septic paperwork, or just point at the yard. We will walk it and talk feasibility, in English o en español.

outdoor-living.local_heading: The yard is why you moved here
intro_paragraphs: Backyards in Southwest Ranches are not backyards. They are paddocks, pastures, orchards, pool decks and whatever else fits on an acre or five, and the outdoor living projects follow that scale: a covered terrace deep enough to sit out a summer storm, a summer kitchen that actually cooks, a pergola over a lounge near the water feature, a paver drive long enough to need lighting. Owners in Sunshine Ranches and Stone Creek at Sunshine Ranches spend more time outside than most South Floridians, and they build accordingly.

Outdoor projects pull in more agencies than indoor ones. The Town of Southwest Ranches permits the structures and inspects them; its engineering side handles right-of-way use permits and the fill, excavation and grading approvals that protect floodplain storage; Broward County licenses the removal or relocation of protected trees; and anything with a roof or an opening needs High-Velocity Hurricane Zone product approvals, since Broward shares the HVHZ with Miami-Dade. Add the town's twenty-five-plus miles of right-of-way trails, which are not a place to park a dumpster.

The difference between an outdoor room and a patio is everything you cannot see once it is finished. Pergola and trellis footings are engineered for wind uplift rather than guessed. Gas, water and electrical runs to a summer kitchen are permitted and inspected. Terraces are pitched to move water away from the slab, not toward it. Sites stay tidy because sound and dust travel differently across open land, and horses have opinions. Fixed written scope, daily supervision, licensed and insured under Lic. CGC1539072.

scope_items.desc: Permitted propane, water and power out to the terrace, weather-rated cabinetry and stone, and a hood arrangement that suits a real grill rather than a display.

scope_items.name: Long driveways and approaches

scope_items.name: Facade work and re-roofing
scope_items.desc: Exterior restoration, color changes and re-roof coordination, sequenced so scaffolding, tile delivery and the new terrace do not fight each other for the same week.

scope_items.name: Impact openings to the outside
scope_items.desc: Sliding walls, French doors and windows carrying HVHZ approvals, installed so the terrace and the house finally behave like one room.

faqs.q: Does a pergola or outdoor kitchen need permits out here?
faqs.a: Yes, on both. The structure needs a building permit from the Town, and the propane, water and electrical runs need their own trade permits and inspections. Depending on placement and grading, the engineering side may also want a fill and grading review. That sounds like a lot of paperwork for a grill and a roof, and it is. The alternative is a structure that becomes debris in September.

faqs.q: Can I take down a tree that is in the way?
faqs.a: Not automatically. Broward County's tree preservation ordinance requires a license to remove or relocate a protected tree, it reaches countywide except where a city's own rules are at least as strict, and the Town has landscape requirements of its own. The usual outcome is a design change rather than a fight: shift the terrace, float a deck around the roots, or relocate the tree instead of losing it. We will tell you plainly which trees are worth designing around and which have a real case for removal.

faqs.q: How do you get materials and equipment onto an acreage property without wrecking it?
faqs.a: Carefully, and with a plan agreed before day one. Access here usually means a narrow private drive, a swale that was never built for a loaded truck, and a right-of-way trail used by riders and walkers. We map the delivery route, lay protection where the ground is soft, stage material away from the trail and the septic field, and repair anything we mark up. Right-of-way work gets its own permit from the Town.

faqs.q: Should the outdoor kitchen run on propane?
faqs.a: Usually, since a natural gas main is not a given out here. A buried or screened tank can feed the grill, the side burner, a pizza oven, the pool heater and a standby generator off one fill, which is tidier than a row of cylinders. Placement follows setback rules and gets permitted, and we size the line for everything you might add later rather than only for what you are buying today.

faqs.q: What does a full outdoor living build run?
faqs.a: Two things drive it: how much roof you want and how many utilities have to travel to get there. A stone terrace with lighting sits at one end. At the other is a fully roofed outdoor room with a summer kitchen, a propane run, a water line, a panel extension and drainage engineered into the grade, on a property where those runs are long. We walk it, specify it, and hand you a fixed written price.
